thesis: An eminence-discounted Dragon deck whose engine is the ARRIVAL, not the attack: cost reduction lands two Dragons in one turn, Miirym and Lathliss turn each arrival into several, and Terror of the Peaks, Dragon Tempest and Scourge of Valkas price every arrival in damage — and V6 wraps that turn in flash so it can be taken on somebody else's.

stages.label: THE FIVE-COLOUR TOLL, PAID TWICE
stages.what_it_does:
Everything downstream is gated on a nine-mana commander and a curve of six-drops in five colours, and the deck pays that toll twice over: 32 land entries / 35 copies, then 23 ramp copies against strategy:deckbuilding.ratios' 10-12, which deck-audit calls OVER. That is a build choice rather than a defect — eminence discounts GENERIC mana and five colours need fixing — but deck-audit still reads mana-base UNDER at 35 copies against 36-38, and colour-sources UNDER by nine on the worst colour, which mana-analysis names as black: 21 sources with rocks and dorks against a yardstick of 30, on-curve 0.729 where every other colour is 0.822 or better.

The ramp itself works. 'Ramp or fixing drawn' assembles in 0.906 of 10,000 goldfish runs at mean turn 2.223, and mean available mana is 5.948 at turn five. Land drops are where it frays: 0.756 at turn four, 0.615 at turn five, and 12 of 35 lands enter tapped (34%).

Five sources here are RESTRICTED, and deck-facts names them: Cavern of Souls, Delighted Halfling, Desolation of Smaug, Maelstrom of the Spirit Dragon and Unclaimed Territory pay for SPELLS only. That is the right shape for this deck and the wrong shape for the colour maths — they accelerate toward a Dragon without ever paying a coloured activation. Desolation of Smaug sits in this stage rather than in output because its four Dragon-only mana is why it is in the 99; deck-audit prices it as the deck's one single point of failure, a one-card component at 0.170 assembled.

The 2026-09-17 rescan put four true fetches in and V6 moved one Forest to one Mountain, which is the pip load talking: 31 cards want {R} for 48 red pips, against 17 cards and 19 green.

evidence.note: all 17 members of the Mana city are lands of mine
all 15 members of the Mana II city are lands of mine; the map splits one landbase in two and neither half means anything the other does not
5 of the 11-card Ramp city are my mana dorks; the other 6 are the Treasure Dragons I filed under fuel, so the map cannot tell a dork from a Dragon that happens to make Treasure
Farseek, Nature's Lore and Skyshroud Claim are 3 of the 5-card Tutors city, filed there because they say 'search your library'; in this deck they are lands
4 of the 5-card Value city are my rocks; the fifth, Dragon's Hoard, I filed under fuel for its gold counters
Desolation of Smaug files with the Dragons, because its loudest text is 3 damage to each non-Dragon creature rather than the four Dragon-only mana it is here for

8 cards carry it against 5 ramp:rock and 2 ramp:land — the ramp is a board, not a pile of artifacts, and every dork is a creature an opponent can kill. Three of the eight (Gadrak, Ganax, Goldspan Dragon) are Treasure Dragons I filed under fuel, so only five of them are in this stage

stages.label: THE PRICE CUT, LIVE FROM TURN ONE
stages.what_it_does:
The first thing that has to happen is a Dragon costing less than it says. Eminence is the only part of this engine an opponent cannot answer: The Ur-Dragon discounts other Dragon spells {1} FROM THE COMMAND ZONE, live on turn one with nothing on the battlefield to remove. Stack 007 step 8 rules it, citing 601.2f, and prices Lathliss at {3}{R}{R} rather than her printed {4}{R}{R} — 'a cost reduction is not optional and the printed {4}{R}{R} is not payable as written'. The four cards here stack on top of it: Dragonlord's Servant and Dragonspeaker Shaman are Dragon-specific, Urza's Incubator and Herald's Horn name a creature type as they enter.

What this stage buys is not one cheap Dragon, it is TWO IN ONE TURN, which is the assumption every trigger downstream is priced against — a six-drop at {3}{R}{R} plus a four-drop is nine mana instead of eleven.

Measured: 'Cost reducer drawn' assembles in 0.521 of 10,000 runs, 0.421 by turn six, mean turn 3.26 — 0.670 and 0.558 with tutors counted. 'Reducer + ramp assembled (the turn-5-Ur-Dragon hand)' is 0.462 / 0.337. So roughly half the deck's games are played at full price.

Note what this stage does NOT buy. The commander itself is on the battlefield by turn six in 0.333 of runs, mean cast turn 6.881, median 7, and never arrives at all in 2,277 of 10,000. Eminence is doing this deck's ignition from a zone the game will not let anyone touch; the body is a bonus. That is also why no card here is a single point of failure — the one piece that must be live cannot be removed, and the other four are redundant with each other.

evidence.note: step 8 rules that Lathliss's total cost is locked in before any of it is paid, minus all cost reductions (601.2f), and that with eminence active from the command zone the cost paid is {3}{R}{R} — five mana, not six
all five sit in the 15-card Insurance city — but so do seven of my protection cards and three of my conversion cards, so one city holds three stages and agrees with none of them
exactly these five carry it, and the fifth is the commander, whose discount works from the command zone where no role tag can see the difference

stages.label: TREASURE, TWO CANTRIPS THAT COME BACK, AND THE DRAW NOBODY COUNTS
stages.what_it_does:
Once a Dragon has landed the deck needs two things it is short of: mana for the SECOND Dragon the same turn, and cards.

Six Treasure sources cover the first — Atsushi, Gadrak, Ganax, Goldspan Dragon, Old Gnawbone and Smaug the Magnificent. 'A Treasure source drawn' assembles in 0.688 of runs, 0.572 by turn six. Read the hoard as a FLOOR and not a measurement: goldfish meta.treasure_sources_not_modelled names Atsushi, Gadrak and Ganax as sources it cannot see, so 0.438 Treasures at turn six and 1.982 at turn ten are what the other three produce. Treasure is a stockpile rather than a rock — it buys one expensive turn and does not raise mean available mana, which is why it sits here and not in mana.

Cards are the thinner half. deck-audit reads card-advantage UNDER at 4 copies against a floor of 10, and its own note says the count misses Dragon's Hoard and Sunbaked Canyon, which do the job in words the taxonomy has no pattern for. What actually refills: Garruk's Uprising and Temur Ascendancy each draw when a creature with power 4 or greater enters — the same event the output stage is built on, so the engine pays for its own next card — Dragon's Hoard banks a gold counter per Dragon entering and cashes them one at a time, and Breaching and Roiling Dragonstorm are cantrips that RETURN TO HAND when a Dragon enters, so they are recastable rather than spent.

Two tutors sit here because their job is to find the missing piece rather than to ramp: Enlightened Tutor (Panharmonicon, Sneak Attack, the three enchantment payoffs) and Sarkhan's Triumph (any Dragon), both at instant speed. The goldfish models a cast tutor as filling one missing any_of group, which is the gap between every unassisted rate in this model and its assisted twin.

evidence.note: 6 of the 11-card Ramp city are my six Treasure sources and the map groups them exactly as the declaration does; the other five are the mana dorks, which I filed under mana

Breaching Dragonstorm, Roiling Dragonstorm, Garruk's Uprising and Temur Ascendancy file with the Dragons — the map hears the Dragon-typal trigger and the haste grant, not the cantrip and the two draws that are the reason they are in the 99
Enlightened Tutor and Sarkhan's Triumph are 2 of the 5-card Tutors city; the other three are the mana stage's land-ramp sorceries
exactly six cards carry it, matching the declared Treasure component card for card

stages.label: ONE ARRIVAL BECOMES SEVERAL, AND EVERY POINT BECOMES TWO
stages.what_it_does:
The engine proper, in two tiers that multiply different things.

MORE ARRIVALS. Miirym copies every other nontoken Dragon that enters; Lathliss makes a 5/5 for each; Ancient Gold Dragon rolls a d20 on combat damage and makes that many hasty Faerie Dragons; Panharmonicon makes every entry trigger of a permanent you control fire twice; and Sneak Attack and Hellkite Courser buy arrivals the mana never paid for — {R} for anything in hand, and a body that puts the commander in with haste and returns it to the command zone with no tax. The token-versus-nontoken line is the brake the rules already had, and both 001 and 002 had to settle it: token copies do not re-trigger Miirym or Lathliss, so the cascade terminates.

MORE DAMAGE PER POINT. Twinflame Tyrant doubles all damage a source you control deals to an opponent or their permanents, Solphim doubles NONCOMBAT damage only, Thrakkus doubles each Dragon's power when it attacks, and Atarka grants an attacking Dragon double strike. Read against the output stage, Twinflame and Solphim both multiply Terror of the Peaks and Dragon Tempest triggers — the shortest route this list has from a board to a table kill — and NONE of the four is verified: combo_details holds no fully-contained record for any of them, and they appear in no passing stack.

single_point_of_failure is null and that is a judgement, not an omission. Stack 007 is the counterfactual and it is brutal about ONE board: cutting Panharmonicon takes stack 002 from 64 damage in twelve instances to 20 in four, 'its LETHALITY, not just its margin', a 68.75% loss. But deck-audit's single_points_of_failure names only Desolation of Smaug, Panharmonicon sits in no goldfish component, and three of these multiplier routes work without each other.

evidence.note: Panharmonicon doubles Miirym's trigger into two nonlegendary 6/6 hasty Lathliss copies; every later entry is a token and both nontoken clauses exclude tokens, so the cascade stops
the same cast with Panharmonicon removed and nothing else changed: Miirym triggers once, one copy enters, 20 damage in four instances. The measured value of one card on one board
15 Faerie Dragon tokens enter as a single event and Miirym copies none of them — a token is not a nontoken Dragon
Sneak Attack puts Drakuseth in with haste for {R}; the same stack REFUTES it reaching the command zone (903.6 — the command zone is not the hand) and names Hellkite Courser as the card that does
7 of my 10 sit in the 29-card Bodies city alongside all ten output cards; the map cannot separate a multiplier from a payoff, because both are printed in the same Dragon-typal words

THE SHARPEST DISAGREEMENT HERE. Miirym, Solphim and Twinflame Tyrant file in the Insurance city beside the cost reducers and Teferi's Protection, because their text reads as a condition on your own stuff. Two of the deck's four damage multipliers therefore share an address with the protection suite

stages.label: WHAT AN ARRIVAL IS WORTH
stages.what_it_does:
What the deck points at a table, and it is priced per ARRIVAL rather than per attack. Terror of the Peaks deals the entering creature's power to any target; Dragon Tempest and Scourge of Valkas deal X where X counts your Dragons and X is recomputed at each trigger's resolution.

Stack 002 measures one Lathliss cast into a four-permanent board at 64 damage in twelve separately-targeted instances — 36 from Terror across six triggers, 28 from Tempest at X = 4,4,5,5,5,5 under optimal ordering — which kills a 32-life seat. Stack 007 step 8 then settles the harder question: every one of those twelve instances reads 'any target', a player is a legal choice for all of them, and aimed at one seat the running total reaches 42 by the eighth instance, so that board CAN kill a player at 40. Stack 001 is the same machine larger: fifteen tokens enter as one event, every Tempest trigger sees X = 17, and 255 damage is available.

Firespitter Whelp is the odd member of the payoff tier and the only one of its four that needs no body to enter: 1 to each opponent whenever you cast a noncreature OR Dragon spell.

The rest is interaction, which deck-audit reads as 11 copies against a floor of 8 but only FOUR classes answered against a floor of five, with graveyard detected as unanswered. Enumerated: Swords to Plowshares and Generous Gift are unconditional single-target answers, Chaos Warp reaches any permanent at instant speed, Crux of Fate is the sweeper, Glorybringer exerts for 4 to a non-Dragon creature, and Steel Hellkite — new in V6 — destroys every nonland permanent of a chosen mana value controlled by a player it dealt combat damage to, once each turn.

evidence.note: 64 damage across twelve instances, 36 Terror + 28 Tempest, killing the 32-life seat
X is recomputed per trigger and each of the fifteen sees 17 Dragons; Dragon Tempest is an Enchantment and does not count itself
step 8 answers (c): stack 002's twelve 'any target' instances reach 42 aimed at a single seat, so a 40-life player is killable off that board
all ten sit in the 29-card Bodies city — the map contains this stage exactly and cannot separate it from conversion, which puts seven of its ten in the same place

seven cards in the 99 carry it and four of them are here — Dragon Tempest, Firespitter Whelp, Glorybringer, Scourge of Valkas. The taxonomy sees an entry payoff whose damage happens to be aimable at a creature and calls it removal; the other three sit in mana, protection and wincon

stages.label: THE ANSWER TO 'I NOW HAVE ZERO RESPONSES'
stages.what_it_does:
Prescription 0241fb6a70f1, after five games at 1W 4L: 'speed without protection or politics makes me the obvious kill target before I can close.' Five of V6's six spell additions land here (the sixth, Steel Hellkite, is in output), and FOUR of the six are castable at instant speed as printed — Stubborn Denial is an instant; Mithril Coat, Transcendent Dragon and Whirlwing Stormbrood have flash; Asceticism and Steel Hellkite do not. What V6 bought is not more protection, it is protection that can be held up.

Asceticism is the only always-on grant in the 99 covering more than one creature: board hexproof, plus regeneration for {1}{G}. Mithril Coat has flash, is itself indestructible and attaches free to a legendary creature as it enters — with 12 legendary creatures here, a three-mana instant that blanks a removal spell. Stubborn Denial is {U} and hard-counters any noncreature spell while you control a 4-power creature — nearly every Dragon here. Transcendent Dragon counters a spell, exiles it and lets you cast it free: a response that is also a body every conversion trigger fires on. Whirlwing Stormbrood protects nothing itself; it makes the rest affordable, because while it is on the battlefield sorceries and Dragon spells have flash, so mana held for a response is never wasted. That thesis is UNVERIFIED — no passing stack touches it.

The five older pieces cost held mana all game, and two read 'if you control a commander' — the commander is on the battlefield by turn six in 0.333 of runs, so Flawless Maneuver and Deflecting Swat usually are not free. interaction_castable_by_turn reads 0.311 / 0.415 / 0.510 on turns four to six, and the model's own note calls that a FLOOR. Thunderbreak Regent only PRICES removal at 3 life; of the twelve it stops nothing.

evidence.note: 7 of my 12 sit in the 15-card Insurance city with the cost reducers and two damage doublers, because the map hears 'a condition on your own stuff' in a reducer and in Teferi's Protection alike

the other 5 — Stubborn Denial, Transcendent Dragon, Whirlwing Stormbrood, Deflecting Swat, Thunderbreak Regent — file with the Dragons, because a counterspell printed on a Dragon body and a redirect both read as board cards. Three of V6's five additions to this stage are therefore at a different address from the other two

nine cards in the 99 carry it and seven are here; the rest of this stage splits across protection:granted (2), protection:redirect, counterspell (2) and buff:attached — five names for one held-up turn

stages.label: PROVEN ON A BOARD, THIN AS A ROUTE
stages.what_it_does:
Two cards, and the thinness is the finding rather than a hole in the model: this deck does not close with a finisher, it closes with the cascade, and every card that does that work is already earning its slot in conversion or output. What is left is the two whose only job is to end the game. Drakuseth, Maw of Flames deals 4 + 3 + 3 to any targets whenever it ATTACKS — an attack trigger, not a cast trigger, so it fires the turn Sneak Attack cheats it in and all 17 damage stands after the mandatory end-step sacrifice (stack 005). Scourge of the Throne untaps all attacking creatures and adds a combat phase the first time it attacks the player with the most life, which is the one card here that doubles an already-lethal board rather than building one.

What is checker-passed: stack 001's board kills BOTH opponents; stack 002's kills the 32-life seat with 64 damage and, per 007 step 8, can reach 42 at a single seat and so kill a player at 40; stack 005 lands 17 from an empty board for {R}. What is NOT checker-passed is any line that gets from an ordinary turn six to one of those boards — every stack starts from a board already assembled.

Against the goldfish's one 40-life opponent that never blocks, median kill turn is 7, mean 7.166, with 0.297 by turn six, 0.621 by turn seven and 0.04 of runs never killing by turn ten; mean board power is 14.877 at turn six and 19.887 at turn seven. Read that as an unopposed clock on ONE seat, not a win rate — and read it against the prescription that named being killed first as the problem, because a deck this fast in a goldfish is a deck a table sees coming.

evidence.note: Drakuseth's trigger is an attack trigger; 4+3+3 fires the turn it arrives and it connects for 7, and all 17 stands through the end-step sacrifice
the deck's only checker-passed board that eliminates two opponents at once
both sit in the 29-card Bodies city with every other Dragon; nothing in the map distinguishes a finisher from a body, which is the map being right — in this deck they mostly are the same card

absent_stages.why: RE-VERIFIED against the current 97 entries rather than carried forward from the v1.0.2 model, because the landbase changed twice since. A regex scan for 'sacrific' returns eleven cards and not one is a sacrifice OUTLET. Four fetchlands (Arid Mesa, Bloodstained Mire, Scalding Tarn, Wooded Foothills), Gemstone Mine and Sunbaked Canyon sacrifice THEMSELVES as their own cost; Maelstrom of the Spirit Dragon sacrifices itself to tutor; Gadrak, Ganax and Goldspan Dragon only print the Treasure token's own self-sacrifice reminder; and Sneak Attack's end-step sacrifice is the price of its effect, not a conversion the deck chooses to make. Nothing converts a permanent you already control into anything else. The standing oddity is still Gadrak, the Crown-Scourge — a Treasure per nontoken creature that died this turn, a fodder PAYOFF in a deck with no fodder and no way to kill its own creatures on purpose. The claim is about permanents as an engine cost, not about resources in general; Treasure is of course spent, and that is why there is a fuel stage. Manufacturing a fodder stage to fill the table would misdescribe the deck.

lines.note: Fifteen Faerie Dragon tokens enter as one event, so Dragon Tempest triggers fifteen times and every trigger sees X = 17 (2 pre-existing Dragons + 15 tokens); 255 damage is available at a single target and the 30-life seat dies to the second. The tokens ARE what Tempest counts and what it triggers on, so the arrow is a feed and not a coincidence. This is also the deck's one fully-contained Commander Spellbook line (bracket 3, 'Near-infinite damage'), which the stack upgrades from candidate to fact.

Panharmonicon doubles Miirym, so one Lathliss cast becomes two nonlegendary 6/6 copies, and those entries pay Terror 36 across six instances of 6 — of which 24 is attributable to Miirym's two copies, the other 12 being the wave-1 triggers on Lathliss's own entry, which Miirym did not cause. One-directional: Miirym makes the bodies whose entry Terror prices.

Panharmonicon doubles every trigger in the cascade, because each is caused by a creature entering — Tempest's six instances read 4,4,5,5,5,5 for 28. It multiplies the payoff and not only the bodies, and stack 007 measures the counterfactual on the same board: without it the whole cascade deals 20.

The floor version, and worth an arrow of its own because it is what the deck actually draws: no Panharmonicon, Miirym triggers once, one copy enters, and the cascade totals 20 damage in four instances. 007 rules that 20 does not kill the 32-life seat that 002's 64 does. The same two cards, a 68.75% swing on one artifact.

The deck's only checker-passed arrow that reaches a finisher. {R} puts Drakuseth in with haste, the attack trigger fires the same turn for 4+3+3, it connects for 7, and all 17 stands after the mandatory end-step sacrifice. The same stack refutes this arrow ever pointing at the commander: 903.6, the command zone is not the hand.

A CLAIM, and the null is load-bearing. Stack 007 step 8 rules the rules half — eminence is active from the command zone and Lathliss's locked-in cost is {3}{R}{R} — but 007's own scenario declares the full {4}{R}{R} paid 'so the cascade, not the discount, is what is being measured', and the scenario names no Ur-Dragon on any board. So the discount is verified as a rule and unverified as this deck's route into the cascade. What it would buy: a turn where Lathliss and a four-drop Dragon both land, which is what every trigger count downstream assumes.

The one arrow that runs from the engine back into its own fuel, and it is unverified. Ganax reads 'Whenever Ganax or another Dragon you control enters, create a Treasure token' with no nontoken clause, so Miirym's token copies should each pay a Treasure — which would make the cascade fund its own next cast. 001 and 002 both had to settle the token-versus-nontoken question for Miirym and Lathliss, and neither board contained Ganax.

V6's whole thesis as a single arrow, and nothing verifies it. Whirlwing reads 'You may cast sorcery spells and Dragon spells as though they had flash', so with it on the battlefield the deck can hold up Stubborn Denial and Mithril Coat through a turn cycle and then deploy the cascade on an opponent's end step with the same mana. If it holds, the deck stops choosing between developing and responding — which is exactly the choice prescription 0241fb6a70f1 says it kept losing.

map_disagreements.component: THE CITY NAMES ARE DETERMINISTIC FALLBACKS, NOT READINGS
map_disagreements.why: Every region in deck_map.json carries label: null and a `fallback` generated from role composition, so 'Insurance', 'Bodies' and 'Value' are what the histogram produced rather than what a cartographer saw. That is how a 15-card city holding five cost reducers, seven protection cards and three damage multipliers ends up called 'Insurance', and how one landbase becomes 'Mana' and 'Mana II'. Read the MEMBERSHIP, which is measured; every disagreement below is about which cards sit together and never about what the cluster is called.

map_disagreements.component: city-2 'Bodies' read as an engine part
map_disagreements.why: 29 cards, 30% of the 97 entries, holding members of SIX of my seven stages: output 10, conversion 7, protection 5, fuel 4, wincon 2, mana 1. It is not a stage. Nor is it quite the Dragon city — enumerated against oracle text and type lines, NINE of the 29 mention Dragons nowhere: Chaos Warp, Deflecting Swat, Garruk's Uprising, Generous Gift, Panharmonicon, Sneak Attack, Stubborn Denial, Swords to Plowshares and Temur Ascendancy. What it collects is permanents and spells that act on a board, which is why a payoff layer, a multiplier layer and half the protection suite land in it together. Anyone reading this map as an engine diagram would conclude the deck has one enormous engine and six accessories.

map_disagreements.component: V6'S RESPONSE SUITE — the change the deck was rebuilt for, at two addresses
map_disagreements.why: The six V6 spell additions exist to answer one prescription, and the map splits them three ways. Asceticism and Mithril Coat read as protection text and file in Insurance; Stubborn Denial, Transcendent Dragon and Whirlwing Stormbrood read as a counterspell and two creature bodies and file in Bodies; Steel Hellkite files in Bodies as a Dragon. A reader working from the constellation would see two unrelated additions to an existing protection cluster and four new Dragons, and would never recover the sentence that explains them — four of the six are castable at instant speed as printed (Stubborn Denial, plus flash on Mithril Coat, Transcendent Dragon and Whirlwing Stormbrood), and the fifth, Steel Hellkite, becomes so while Whirlwing is on the battlefield. Only Asceticism is a plain sorcery-speed permanent. That sentence is in no single card's text, which is exactly why the map cannot hold it.

Four cards do one job — multiply damage the engine already deals — and the map gives them two addresses. Solphim and Twinflame Tyrant file in Insurance next to Teferi's Protection and Lightning Greaves, because a replacement effect on damage reads as a condition on your own stuff; Atarka and Thrakkus file in Bodies, because double strike and doubled power are printed on attacking Dragons. The deck's declaration has the same split from the other side: goldfish_targets' COMBAT KILL leg names only Atarka and Thrakkus as multipliers and counts Twinflame Tyrant as a BODY.

Six of the eleven cards in the 'Ramp' city are 4-to-7-power flying Dragons — Atsushi, Gadrak, Ganax, Goldspan Dragon, Old Gnawbone, Smaug the Magnificent — sitting beside Birds of Paradise and Ignoble Hierarch because they all make mana. In this engine they are both: the Treasure pays for the second Dragon and the body is itself an arrival the output stage prices. The map cannot file one card twice, and neither can this model; I put them in fuel, which understates them exactly as much as the map's 'Ramp' does.

map_disagreements.component: 'Ramp or fixing drawn' — the widest scatter in the brief
map_disagreements.why: engine-facts' scatter table puts this 12-card component across three cities at 5 / 4 / 3 and marks it incoherent, and it is the component the deck depends on most (0.906 assembled). The split is a taxonomy artefact: a dork is a creature, a rock is an artifact, and Farseek, Nature's Lore and Skyshroud Claim say 'search your library', which is enough to file three land-ramp sorceries beside Enlightened Tutor. All twelve answer one question — can I pay for a six-drop on turn four — and no two of them say it in the same words.

open_questions.question: With Whirlwing Stormbrood // Dynamic Soar on the battlefield, can the deck cast Lathliss, Dragon Queen on an opponent's end step and have the full Miirym / Terror of the Peaks / Dragon Tempest cascade resolve at instant speed — do all the entry triggers behave identically outside your own main phase, and does the Omen half (Dynamic Soar, {2}{G}) matter to the line at all?
open_questions.why_it_matters: This is the single claim V6 was built on: five of six additions are instant-speed and Whirlwing is the card that makes the DECK instant-speed, so the pilot stops choosing between developing and holding up a response. It is the `protection -> conversion` arrow in this model, it carries verified_by: null, and no passing stack touches it. If it holds, the protection stage stops being a tax on the pivot turn and becomes free; if it does not, V6 added four responses the deck still cannot afford to hold.

open_questions.question: Hellkite Courser and The Ur-Dragon: walk the full turn. Courser enters, its ETB puts the commander from the command zone onto the battlefield with haste, both attack — does The Ur-Dragon's own attack trigger ('draw that many cards, then you may put a permanent card from your hand onto the battlefield') fire, and does the return to the command zone at the beginning of the next end step leave commander tax at zero for a later hard cast?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Stack 005 REFUTES Sneak Attack as a commander-cheat and names Hellkite Courser, in its own resolution prose, as 'the card that actually does what the frame claimed' — and then never resolves it. V6 deliberately kept Courser rather than cutting it. The goldfish says why it matters: the commander is on the battlefield by turn six in 0.333 of runs, mean cast turn 6.881, and never arrives at all in 2,277 of 10,000. Courser may be this deck's real commander route and nothing in the evidence base measures it.

open_questions.question: Do Twinflame Tyrant and Solphim, Mayhem Dominus both apply to the same damage event — a Dragon Tempest or Terror of the Peaks trigger aimed at an opponent — for four times the printed damage, and if so who chooses the order the two replacement effects apply in (CR 616.1)? Resolve on a board with one doubler, then both, and state the multiplier exactly.
open_questions.why_it_matters: Carried forward unanswered from the v1.0.2 model and still the largest unmeasured quantity here. Neither card appears in a passing stack, in a fully-contained combo line, or in a goldfish leg that treats it as a multiplier. If both apply, stack 002's board reads 256 rather than 64 and 007's ceiling — that 64 cannot kill both seats, since 64 < 72 — stops being a ceiling.

open_questions.question: Re-run the goldfish with the V6 protection additions declared (Asceticism, Mithril Coat, Stubborn Denial, Transcendent Dragon added to 'Protection held for the big turn') and with the two cut cards removed from the ENTRY KILL and Dragon-restricted-mana legs. What do 'Protection held for the big turn' and interaction_castable_by_turn read then, against the current 0.665 / 0.557 and 0.311 / 0.415 / 0.510?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The declared protection group names SIX cards and every one of them predates V6, so the 0.665 the audit prints is a rate for the suite the pilot already judged insufficient — it cannot see the four cards bought to fix it. goldfish_metrics' own meta.interaction_suite_counted already lists all four, so the model can read them and only the declaration is behind. Until this is re-run, no figure in this deck's record prices the change that was made today.

open_questions.question: Can this deck actually hold {4}{U}{U} up for Transcendent Dragon on the turn it wants to pivot? Blue is 20 total sources against a 22 yardstick with on-curve 0.881, but the card is six mana and the cascade turn is the same turn.
open_questions.why_it_matters: Transcendent Dragon is the most expensive response in the deck and the only one that is also a body the engine triggers on, so its value is entirely a question of whether the mana exists twice. interaction_castable_by_turn is 0.510 at turn six and the model's own note calls that a FLOOR because it spends rather than holds — which means the figure that would answer this does not exist yet in either direction.

proposed_goldfish_edits.target: Dragon-restricted mana drawn (counts for nothing in mana_analysis, everything for casting a Dragon)
proposed_goldfish_edits.change: Remove 'Sarkhan, Fireblood' from the single any_of leg, leaving ['Desolation of Smaug'] — or delete the target and fold Desolation of Smaug into a note, since a one-card target is a hypergeometric statement about one card.
proposed_goldfish_edits.why: Sarkhan, Fireblood was cut in V6 (2026-09-20). deck-audit already prices the component as size 1 and lists the name under not_in_deck, so the 0.170 rate is correct — but the declaration still reads as a two-card group, and a reader comparing 0.170 against a two-card leg will conclude the deck is unlucky rather than that it has one card.

proposed_goldfish_edits.target: THE ENTRY KILL (UNVERIFIED — no passing stack): a per-dragon DAMAGE payoff AND a way to put several Dragons on the battlefield at once
proposed_goldfish_edits.change: Remove 'Sarkhan, Fireblood' and 'Utvara Hellkite' from need[1]. Both were cut (Sarkhan in V6, Utvara Hellkite in V6), leaving Ancient Gold Dragon, Lathliss and Miirym.
proposed_goldfish_edits.why: Two of the five names in that leg cannot be drawn. The measured 0.179 / 0.109 is arithmetically correct — a card not in the deck is simply never drawn — but the declaration overstates the leg by 40% of its names, and this is the target the deck's primary kill is measured through.

proposed_goldfish_edits.target: THE ENTRY KILL (UNVERIFIED — no passing stack): a per-dragon DAMAGE payoff AND a way to put several Dragons on the battlefield at once
proposed_goldfish_edits.change: Consider ADDING Sneak Attack and Hellkite Courser to need[1] after the two cuts above, as a separate decision from the correction.
proposed_goldfish_edits.why: Both literally put a Dragon onto the battlefield outside the mana cost — Sneak Attack any creature in hand for {R}, Courser the commander from the command zone — which is the leg's stated job, and stack 005 proves Sneak Attack doing it. Proposed as a SEPARATE edit because it moves the rate UP and the correction above moves it down, and a human should not be handed one number that conceals two changes.

proposed_goldfish_edits.target: Protection held for the big turn
proposed_goldfish_edits.change: Add Asceticism, Mithril Coat, Stubborn Denial and Transcendent Dragon to the six-card any_of leg, making it ten.
proposed_goldfish_edits.why: Every one of the six currently named predates V6, and none of V6's five additions to the protection stage is present — so the 0.665 assembled / 0.557 by turn six that deck-audit prints is a rate for the suite the pilot judged insufficient after five games. goldfish_metrics meta.interaction_suite_counted already names all four, so the model reads them and only the declaration is stale. This is the single edit without which nothing in the record measures what changed today.

proposed_goldfish_edits.target: Protection held for the big turn
proposed_goldfish_edits.change: Consider a SECOND, separate target — 'A response castable at instant speed' — over Boros Charm, Deflecting Swat, Flawless Maneuver, Heroic Intervention, Mithril Coat, Stubborn Denial, Teferi's Protection, Transcendent Dragon and Whirlwing Stormbrood // Dynamic Soar.
proposed_goldfish_edits.why: 'Protection held for the big turn' and 'can I respond on somebody else's turn' are different questions and V6 was bought to answer the second. Lightning Greaves and Asceticism are always-on and belong in the first but not the second; Whirlwing Stormbrood belongs in the second and protects nothing. Splitting them is what makes the next measurement readable.

proposed_goldfish_edits.target: Payoff + a castable dragon by mid-game
proposed_goldfish_edits.change: Add Steel Hellkite, Transcendent Dragon and Whirlwing Stormbrood // Dynamic Soar to need[1], the castable-Dragon leg.
proposed_goldfish_edits.why: All three are Dragons that arrived in V6 and all three are exactly what that leg asks for — a body the payoff tier can trigger on, at five or six mana. Steel Hellkite is {6} colourless and so is castable in the widest range of hands of any Dragon in the 99. The leg currently names eight cards and none of them is newer than v1.0.2.

proposed_goldfish_edits.target: A Treasure source drawn — six in the 99, of which the model can SPEND only two
proposed_goldfish_edits.change: Relabel to name three, not two: '… of which the model can SPEND three'. Leave the six-card leg unchanged.
proposed_goldfish_edits.why: Carried forward unapplied from the v1.0.2 model and still true: goldfish_metrics meta.treasure_sources_not_modelled names exactly three — Atsushi, Gadrak, Ganax — leaving three of six modelled. The 'two' dates from v1.0.0, when the unmodelled list was five. A label that misstates its own model is how a reader turns a floor into a ceiling.

proposed_goldfish_edits.target: THE COMBAT KILL (UNVERIFIED — no passing stack): a Dragon-damage MULTIPLIER AND a Dragon to attack with
proposed_goldfish_edits.change: Move Twinflame Tyrant from need[1] (the castable-Dragon leg) to need[0] (the multiplier leg), making the legs 3 and 7 rather than 2 and 8. Do not add it to both.
proposed_goldfish_edits.why: Carried forward unapplied. Twinflame Tyrant reads 'If a source you control would deal damage to an opponent or a permanent an opponent controls, it deals double that damage instead' — a Dragon-damage multiplier by the same test that admitted Atarka (double strike) and Thrakkus (double power), and unconditional where those two need an attack. It is currently counted as a BODY. Moving rather than adding matters: a card in both legs of an AND can satisfy the whole target by itself.
